curation.notes: Paper describes a coarse-grained molecular dynamics model of the axon membrane skeleton (actin rings connected by spectrin filaments) used to compute stiffness via radial expansion. No traditional force-extension pulling of a single molecule; the 'pulling' is a quasi-static radial expansion of the entire network to measure pressure vs. strain. Classified as CG-GO due to the use of simplified, structure-based potentials (harmonic, LJ, FENE) for a cytoskeletal network. Event type is A-stretching (measuring elastic modulus of the network). Topology is parallel (spectrin filaments act as parallel load-bearing elements between actin rings). Experimental comparison is to the authors' own AFM indentation measurements.

The second study (Brownian dynamics pulling) is a separate class (AN-*) and is not a biomolecular pulling simulation; a second record is not created as per instruction to return empty array if no pulling simulation.
